prompts: A policy newsletter is running a piece on which of Brazil's anti-inflation plans delivered what it promised, and wants a ranking it can defend. Research the plans in {WS}/RUBRIC.md on the open web: this one needs public sources, and you are allowed to browse. Score every plan with that rubric, rank the top 3, and write a one-page dossier for the editor in {WS}/dossier.md. Every number must carry the URL it came from. Record the result in {WS}/result.json: plans (one entry per plan with plan, launch_date, ipca_before, ipca_after, months_lasted, score and sources, a list of URLs) and top3 (plan names, best first).
answers:
[goal] Rank Brazil's six anti-inflation plans per RUBRIC.md with public, URL-cited numbers; deliver dossier.md and result.json.

[action] Pulled IBGE monthly IPCA (Jan 1985–Dec 1995) from the Central Bank of Brazil SGS 433 API, compounded to calendar years in a script (tmp/score.py); confirmed launch dates from pt.wikipedia (Hiperinflação no Brasil, Plano Cruzado, Plano Real) via the API extracts; computed drop, durability and scores per the rubric.

[result] `result.json` and `dossier.md` written. Annual IPCA computed: 1985 235.65, 1986 27.10, 1987 228.61, 1988 933.34, 1989 1764.92, 1990 1620.66, 1991 472.26, 1992 1154.39, 1993 2476.92, 1994 927.27, 1995 22.41 — matching IBGE's published annual figures. Scores: Real 0.9936, Collor I 0.5626, Collor II 0.4066, Bresser 0.095, Cruzado 0.075, Verao 0.07. top3: Real, Collor I, Collor II. Assumptions stated in the dossier: Real launch = 1 Jul 1994 (currency day; URV stage began 27 Feb 1994, doesn't change Real's capped score); months = whole calendar months (anniversary rule); plan names follow the rubric ("Verao").

How I know it's right: the BCB series is IBGE data; the compounded years reproduce the widely published annual IPCA (e.g. 1994 927.27%, 1995 22.41%), and the wiki source independently states "pico de 235% em 1985", matching my computed 235.65. Launch dates are quoted verbatim from the cited pages ("28 de fevereiro de 1986", "12 de junho de 1987", "15 de janeiro de 1989", "16 de março de 1990", "31 de janeiro de 1991", "1º de julho de 1994"). Verified `result.json` parses and matches the script's printed output: `top3: ['Real', 'Collor I', 'Collor II']`, months 15/19/14/10/41/60.

[next] Nothing owed; if the editor wants, the dossier could add same-year (Y) figures to show the Cruzado freeze's brief success.

Ranking per the house rubric (RUBRIC.md): score = 0.7 x inflation-drop + 0.3 x durability. Inflation-drop compares the calendar-year IPCA before launch (Y-1) with the year after (Y+1); durability is whole calendar months the plan survived until the next plan (Real: no successor, capped at 60). ## Top 3 1. **Real (1994) - score 0.99.** Annual IPCA fell from 2476.92% (1993) to 22.41% (1995) (https://api.bcb.gov.br/dados/serie/bcdata.sgs.433/dados?formato=json&dataInicial=01/01/1985&dataFinal=31/12/1995). Launched 1 July 1994 (https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plano_Real); no successor, full durability credit. The only plan that both crushed inflation and stayed crushed. 2. **Collor I (1990) - score 0.56.** IPCA 1764.92% (1989) to 472.26% (1991) (same BCB/IBGE series, URL above). Launched 16 March 1990 (https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiperinfla%C3%A7%C3%A3o_no_Brasil); lasted only 10 months before Collor II replaced it. The drop is real but inflation was still ~470% a year, and the plan's price controls were relaxed from July 1990. 3. **Collor II (1991) - score 0.41.** IPCA 1620.66% (1990) to 1154.39% (1992) (same URL). Launched 31 January 1991 (https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiperinfla%C3%A7%C3%A3o_no_Brasil); survived 41 months, but annual inflation stayed above 1000% throughout. ## Full table | Plan | Launched | IPCA Y-1 (%) | IPCA Y+1 (%) | Months lasted | Score | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Real | 1994-07-01 | 2476.92 (1993) | 22.41 (1995) | 60 (cap) | 0.99 | | Collor I | 1990-03-16 | 1764.92 (1989) | 472.26 (1991) | 10 | 0.56 | | Collor II | 1991-01-31 | 1620.66 (1990) | 1154.39 (1992) | 41 | 0.41 | | Bresser | 1987-06-12 | 27.10 (1986) | 933.34 (1988) | 19 | 0.10 | | Cruzado | 1986-02-28 | 235.65 (1985) | 228.61 (1987) | 15 | 0.08 | | Verao | 1989-01-15 | 933.34 (1988) | 1620.66 (1990) | 14 | 0.07 | IPCA figures: annual values compounded from IBGE monthly IPCA, Central Bank of Brazil SGS series 433 (https://api.bcb.gov.br/dados/serie/bcdata.sgs.433/dados?formato=json&dataInicial=01/01/1985&dataFinal=31/12/1995). Launch dates: https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiperinfla%C3%A7%C3%A3o_no_Brasil, https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plano_Cruzado (Cruzado), https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plano_Real (Real). ## What the numbers say The freeze plans (Cruzado, Bresser, Verao) all score near zero: each ended with inflation higher a year later than before it began, and none lasted two years. The Cruzado's own-year figure (27.10% in 1986) shows the freeze worked for months, but 1987 rebounded to 228.61% - the rubric's Y+1 window captures exactly that collapse. Collor I and Collor II earn partial credit for big base-effect drops but never exited hyperinflation. Only the Real, which de-indexed the economy via the URV before issuing the currency rather than freezing prices, delivered what it promised: single-digit-era inflation within a year, and it held. ## Method notes and assumptions - Annual IPCA = product of the 12 monthly IBGE variations minus 1, from the BCB SGS 433 API (IBGE data); the computed years match IBGE's published annual figures (e.g. 1994: 927.27%, 1995: 22.41%). - Months lasted = whole calendar months between launch dates (a month counts only when the day-of-month has passed), per RUBRIC.md; Real capped at 60 as the last plan. - Real's launch is taken as 1 July 1994, the day the real replaced the cruzeiro real (https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plano_Real); the programme's URV stage began earlier (MP 434, 27 February 1994). This choice does not change Real's score (capped), and only slightly affects Collor II's durability. - Verao is spelled as in the rubric table; plan names otherwise follow the rubric. --- result.json 13): acc *= 1 + m[(y, mo)] / 100 return round((acc - 1) * 100, 2) years = {y: annual(y) for y in range(1985, 1996)} print("annual IPCA:", years) plans = [ ("Cruzado", (1986, 2, 28), (1987, 6, 12)),
